title: kv quant twilight notes
content:
Evening quick notes + running TODOs — trying to capture the stray ideas before I forget. Mostly small experiments around KV-cache interaction after 4-bit quant and some prompt-behavior observations.

Date: 2026-03-16
Context: local devbox (dgx2-sim, 2xA100 emu), running tiny eval harness against conversational workload (mix of short
assistant-turns and long context summaries). Goal: see when 4-bit (nf4) with blockwise-kv leads to token-degeneration across repeated prefixes.

What I ran today (short):
- baseline: fp16 model variant v2026-03-10, batch_size=1, no kv-cache warming, 128 context warmup tokens. 1200 tokens/sec peak.
- q4_nf4 + blockwise-kv (block=64): slightly lower peak ~980 t/s, occasional token repetition at step ~350 for prompt family B.
- q4_nf4 + blockwise-kv + prefix-warmup (2048 prefill): repeats reduced but latency spike on first chunk.
- q4_hybrid (kv stored fp16, activations 4-bit) experiment: promising — repetition gone for family B, throughput similar to q4_nf4 baseline.

Quick numbers (very noisy):
- baseline fp16: PPL(avg)=12.1, avg latency per token=4.2ms
- q4_nf4: PPL(avg)=13.8, avg latency per token=5.1ms, repetition incidents=3/30 runs
- q4_nf4 + warmup: PPL(avg)=13.4, avg latency per token=6.8ms (first-token spike), reps=1/30
- q4_hybrid: PPL(avg)=12.5, avg latency per token=5.3ms, reps=0/30

Interpretation / hypothesis:
- Quantizing both activations and KV structures to 4-bit introduces small distribution shifts that the autoregressive sampler compounds after many steps. Blockwise-kv aggravates it when blocks are small (loss of cross-block precision?).
- Keeping KV in fp16 but quantizing weights/activations (q4_hybrid) appears to retain steady-state probability mass better while preserving most speed/cost gains. Could be a useful default for latency-sensitive inference where repetition is a concern.

Immediate TODOs (prio order):
1) Re-run q4_hybrid across prompt family A/B/C with 100 random seeds and log sample entropy curves (metric: sample-entropy delta across tokens). Target: tonight or tomorrow morning.
2) Try block=128 and block=256 for q4_nf4 to isolate block-size effect. (Low effort)
3) Add tiny temperature sweep (0.7, 0.8, 1.0) to see whether sampler temperature masks quant effects.
4) Instrument KV-read variance: store per-token kv norm and compute drift over time. Create quick viz.
5) Draft short note for infra folks: recommend offering "kv-fp16" as a quantization compatibility flag for dedicated pools serving long-context chat apps.

Prompt sets used (abridged):
- family A (short-turn support): system: "You are a concise assistant. Answer in 1-2 sentences." user: "Explain LRU cache in 2 lines."
- family B (repetition-prone long): multi-turn history ~10 pairs, user asks to summarize and continue. This is where repeats occurred.
- family C (creative): single long user ~1024 tokens asking a narrative continuation.

Command snippets / notes to self:
- run harness: ./local_eval/run_minibench.sh --model q4_hybrid --dataset conv-familyB --seeds 0..99 --out results/q4h-familyB-20260316.log
- kv norm extraction: python tools/extract_kv_norms.py --trace results/q4h-familyB-20260316.log --out norms/q4h-familyB-20260316.csv
- quick viz: vega-lite spec in /home/diego/scratch/kv-viz.json (very crude)

Questions / open unknowns:
- Is the repetition mechanism purely numeric drift, or does quantization change attention distribution sparsity? Need attention-map diffs.
- How much does per-layer quantization scale matter (e.g., quantize only middle layers vs first/final)?
- Could key/value compression (product quantization) be combined with fp16 KV to save mem without changing distribution?

Notes for next sync with Maya/Samir:
- Show 2 example runs: one q4_nf4 that repeats and one q4_hybrid that doesn't (same seed and prompt).
- Proposal: add a new "kv_format" flag in config with options ["auto", "fp16", "q4_block"] and default auto -> choose fp16 for contexts > 1024 tokens. Need perf tradeoff table.

Mini retrospective (today):
- Wins: found a plausible mitigation (kv fp16) without throwing away quantization benefits.
- Friction: warmup reduces repeats but introduces latency spikes; not acceptable for small-snippet latency SLOs.

Random TODOs (personal):
- write up 1-pager for infra before EOD Monday (risk: committed changes to model pipeline).
- remind infra: GPU memory accounting for hybrid mode.

That’s it for tonight — will pick up with larger statistical runs tomorrow. If I forget, ping me in #aml-kv or DM.

-- Diego
